measurements.description_left_edges: 11 distinct x positions; the one-row inline descriptors start anywhere from 121.44 to 143.71 mm, a 22.3 mm ragged inner edge
measurements.baseline_grid: none shared: 15 pt name rows, 14 pt ingredient lines, 18.2 pt section gaps, and 7/5/9 pt gaps are not multiples of one unit

remove: The dotted leaders. Pull every price in to a short hop (about 1 em) after its name or descriptor, as DESIGN_THEORY_BRIEF sections 2.3 and 5 require ('no leaders', 'no row may exceed 40% eye travel'). Of the 12 remaining devices, the leaders are the one doing a job the layout should do instead.
top_problem: The reading layer is a 104 mm single-column list with prices pushed to the far right and held there by 12-66 mm leaders. That breaks the brief's binding rule for inline prices (the worst row has 0.68 eye travel). The art, a sun disc plus agave, is generic Mexican: it fails the substitution test and has nothing of Iowa City in it. The boldest missing idea is an art gesture that fuses the two places, for example a horizon where the agave field turns into Iowa's cut-paper corn rows or the Old Capitol dome under the same sun, so that no other cantina could use the page.
fixes: Remove the leaders and set each price a short hop (about 1 em) after the name or descriptor. At the same time, drop the price to 11 pt at the name's size in the muted ink, so that no row goes over 40% eye travel and prices stop outranking names (criterion 3, currently far-right at 0.68).

Put every line on one baseline grid (for example 7 pt: name rows 14, ingredient lines 14, gaps 7/14/21, section gap 28) and stack the one-row descriptors under the name, or on a fixed tab at one x. This removes the 11-position ragged inner edge (121.44-143.71 mm) that is the page's most visible alignment flaw.

Put the wordmark and the vertical venue line on one axis (58.56 vs 60.23 mm today), cap-align the top of CANTINA with the H2 cap line (0.56 mm off), and give the empty 42 x 100 mm wordmark lane below CANTINA a job, or narrow the lane and widen the gutter so the reading column shortens its measure.

Cut the tracked-caps load: set item names in title case (Fraunces 600, 11-12 pt, no tracking) so H2, H3 and the glass labels are the only caps levels, and raise H2 to at least 1.5x the name size so the section step reads at a squint.

Rework the art into one torn-paper grammar: the speckled noise on the sun reads as digital dither next to the flat vector agave. Give every shape the same torn fibre edge and the same grain, and bring in one Iowa element so the collage passes the substitution test (criteria 15 and 16).

remove: The dotted leaders (17 of them). Use two short columns or an inline price a short hop after the name instead. The leaders turn the page into a price list and are the heaviest texture in the reading layer; ref-01 has none.
top_problem: The typography has no hierarchy by contrast; every level is loud. Item names are 11 pt, 600 weight, tracked caps. They share the heads' face and case, so H2, H3, names and the DM Sans serve labels all shout in tracked capitals. The bilingual heads make Spanish the grey, light half and English the black, bold half, which demotes the venue's language in its own cantina. The heads use two weights and two inks per head level, and AGAVE and BRANDY break the pattern. Ref-01 puts light, airy names under a single monumental wordmark. This page is a dense slab of bold caps beside a good wordmark. Boldest missing idea: the bilingual structure is the concept, but it is set as a colour toggle. Give Spanish and English equal status as a typographic pair (for example Spanish in Fraunces italic and English in roman, same ink and weight) so the two languages become the ownable Iowa City and Mexico fusion the brief asks for.
fixes: Set item names in title case, Fraunces 500 at 11.5 pt with little or no tracking, so tracked caps are kept only for the H3 labels and the wordmark, and the names read as the calm reading layer the brief requires.

Rebuild the bilingual heads so both languages carry equal weight and one ink: Spanish in Fraunces italic and English in roman at the same weight, or Spanish first at full ink. Give AGAVE and BRANDY the same two-part treatment (for example AGAVE · AGAVE is wrong, so use one-word heads styled as a single run matching the Spanish half), so every H3 follows one rule.

Remove the leaders and bring prices within 40% eye travel. Use a 2-column split for Beer/Wine/Spirits (the heads can go on two lines, as ref-01 stacks them) or put the price about 1 em after the name in a lighter weight, which also ends the 'Cognac VSOP 18' age-statement risk.

Drop the DM Sans bold serve labels (ROCKS, COUPE) into Fraunces small caps or italic at the ingredient-line weight, and cut the Margarita-only tasting line, so every cocktail has the same two-line anatomy and ends with a clean rag (no dangling 'fresh lime ·' breaks).

Remove the echo descriptions set right after the name ('BLANCO TEQUILA blanco tequila', 'COGNAC VSOP VSOP Cognac'), or move them into an aligned second column as ref-01 does for wine, so the inline one-row format stops producing 11 ragged description start points.

lens: palette, contrast over the art, price and number styling

margins_mm.note: left is the full-bleed art rail and exempt; the reading column's three measurable sides are within 0.17 mm

measurements.description_left_edges_pt_one_row: 11 distinct x values (344-407 pt): the draft words float at a different x on every one-row line, so there is a ragged mid-column
measurements.item_gaps_pt: 7.0 between cocktails, 4.99 between one-row items (constant within each type)
measurements.rows_over_40pct: 4 on letter, all with dotted leaders
measurements.price_vs_name: prices are Fraunces 600 at 12.5 pt against names at 11 pt, so prices are 14% larger at the same weight

remove: The dotted leaders. At 2.72:1 they are the faintest ink on the page and they only patch a far-right price column that the brief (section 5, binding) forbids. Set each price a 1 em hop after its item's text in the muted ink, and the leaders and 0.68 eye travel both disappear.
top_problem: The palette and art are handsome but borrowed. Sunset disc, agave and terracotta hills pass for any Southwest cantina and fail the substitution test, with nothing in the idea that fuses Mexico and Iowa City. The reading layer shouts in bold tracked caps: names and prices are both 600-weight caps, and prices are larger than names and sit at the far edge of a 104 mm measure. This is the price styling the brief's house grammar rejects (plain names, price a short hop right, same size, no leaders).
fixes: Bring prices inline, about 1 em after the last word of each row's name or draft text, at 11 pt in #4F4238 tabular lining figures (not 12.5 pt 600 ink). Delete the leaders so no row exceeds 0.40 eye travel on letter or phone.

Set item names in title case, Fraunces 500-600 at 11-11.5 pt without .11em tracking. 'BROWN BUTTER OLD FASHIONED' breaks the tracked-caps-only-for-labels-of-3-words-or-fewer rule, and caps names plus caps prices plus caps glass labels leave the reading layer no quiet voice.

Stop demoting Spanish to grey-brown 420 weight in the H2s. In a Mexican cantina this reads as a lesser language. Set both halves in one ink and let a lighter weight or italic carry the distinction, or lead with Spanish at full ink. Make 'AGAVE' and 'BRANDY' bilingual or explicitly language-neutral so every H3 follows one pattern.

Unify the image treatment. The sun has a heavy sponge-speckle grain while the agave and hills are near-flat vector fills, so there are two finishes. Put one paper-fibre grain on every art shape and add one Iowa-specific transformation, such as the hill strata cut as Iowa River bluffs or prairie contour, so the art fails the substitution test.

Align the one-row draft words to a single tab stop (for example 282 + 40 mm) or stack them under the name as on the phone, so the 11 floating left edges (344-407 pt) become one column. Lift the terracotta H3 from its 5.19:1 worst pixel toward #86311C (about 6.8:1) for dim-bar reading of 9 pt tracked caps.

remove: the dotted leaders: set every price inline, a short hop after its name, and let a short column carry the price-to-name link
top_problem: This is a clean, well-built copy of ref-02 panel 2 (sun disc, agave, cream ground), not an ownable idea. A gold sun and an agave would suit any Mexican bar in America, and nothing in the art joins Mexico with Iowa City. The boldest missing idea is to make the torn-paper landscape itself the fusion. For example, the agave could rise out of layered Iowa loess hills or cornfield strata, so the collage could not be moved to another city.
fixes: Rebuild the rail art so the torn layers read as Iowa (loess-hill contours or corn-row furrows cut from the same paper), with the agave growing out of them, so no other bar could reuse it; this lifts criteria 15 and 16.
Remove the dotted leaders and set prices inline about 1 em after each name (or narrow the column to about 60% so eye travel drops under 40%), as brief section 5 requires.

Cut the caps load: set item names in title-case Fraunces 600 without tracking, keep tracked caps only for the H3 labels, and move the glass names from the separate DM Sans bold caps into the lighter ingredient line in lowercase italics.

Give the agave leaves real cut-paper craft (torn deckle edges, one inner fold tone, a shadow offset that matches the hills), and replace the digital-noise speckle on the sun with a gold-leaf crackle, so the texture holds up at actual size like the ref-02 painterly panels.

Lighten the flat dark ground block at the foot of the rail, or tear it back, so it frames the agave instead of sitting there as a dead block, and stop one-word descriptions that repeat the item name ('BLANCO TEQUILA blanco tequila') from reading as filler.

measurements.phone_first_screen: about 49% of the first 2250 px is the art crop (a sun segment with its top cut off, 1 agave spike, a green sliver on the left edge and a terracotta sliver in the bottom-right corner). The art meets the paper in a straight horizontal cut, so the phone has no torn edge.
measurements.phone_tail: about 150 px of blank paper below the allergen line, with no closing device

remove: The coarse speckle grain on the gold sun. At phone scale (3x) it turns into blotchy, JPEG-like mottling over half the first screen and fails the texture-at-actual-size test. Use a fine, low-contrast gold-leaf grain, or no grain on the phone art.
top_problem: The phone is a different, lesser menu. It drops the torn page edge, the vertical wordmark and the agave rosette, which carry the concept ('sun behind a torn page'), and it opens with an arbitrary crop full of edge slivers and a ruler-straight art/paper seam. It then runs as a long cream web list where one-row items become two-line stacks with full-width leaders. The boldest missing idea: nothing in the art fuses Iowa City with Mexico (brief section 5). The torn hills could be read as the Iowa River bluffs or prairie under the agave sun, but they only say 'desert sunset', which fails the substitution test against any cantina.
fixes: Re-art-direct the phone hero as its own crop: the full sun disc sitting behind a torn paper edge, with the agave rosette rising into it, and the torn edge running horizontally as the seam into the reading layer. Put no slivers at the frame edges.

On the phone, keep one-row items on one line as print does (name, draft words, price a short hop right; drop the leader where the row fits in 342 px). The stacked name/leader/price plus a separate description line creates a leader wall and doubles echoes like 'BLANCO TEQUILA / blanco tequila' and 'COGNAC VSOP / VSOP Cognac'.

Shorten the print eye travel: set the price about 1 em after the text on cocktail rows, or narrow the item measure to about 220 pt with prices on that edge. This removes the 187 pt Margarita leader and the 0.53-0.68 rows, bringing the page closer to ref-01/ref-04's short-hop pricing.

Fix the phone H2 break so 'CERVEZA Y SIDRA · BEER & CIDER' behaves like the other H2s (for example stack Spanish over English for all four H2s, with no trailing '·'). Rebalance the cocktail ingredient breaks so no line ends on a lone separator ('white rum · fresh lime ·', 'rye · sweet vermouth ·').

Close the phone with the art: bring back the dark ground band and agave tips as a torn-edge footer under the allergen line, so the phone is bracketed by the same collage as the print rail rather than ending in blank paper.

lens: every item and price vs build/draft_doc.json (TEST-1 round 19, Mexican restaurant + cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: Content is honest (14/14 items, 14/14 prices, no taglines, no invented facts). But 10 of the 14 descriptions are placeholders: the three spirits only repeat their names ('BLANCO TEQUILA blanco tequila', 'AÑEJO TEQUILA añejo tequila', 'COGNAC VSOP VSOP Cognac'), and the beer, cider and wine lines are one-word style tags. So half the page reads like a price list with filler, not a cantina menu. The missing beer ABV, wine region and spirit brand is a known data gap with Rob and is not the designer's fault. Echoing the item name is the designer's choice.
problems: Data gap (not the designer's fault; tabulated in proposal.md and doc.json meta.missing): no ABV or brewery for Czech Pilsner, Dry-Hopped IPA, Amber Lager or Dry Cider; no region or producer for Malbec, Pinot Grigio or Brut Rosé; no brand or age for Blanco, Añejo or Cognac VSOP. Criterion 8 cannot pass 80 until Rob answers.

Spirits descriptions are tautologies: each one repeats the item name in lower case. That fails the 'never just repeats the item name' standard and adds a second, pointless text lane to every spirits row.
'VSOP Cognac' is in title case, while every other descriptor is lower case ('blanco tequila', 'dry red wine'). Descriptor voice is inconsistent.

Margarita: the glass label ROCKS is set mid-copy, after 'lime wheel' and before the draft sentence 'Bright and citrus-forward.' So the tasting note looks orphaned under the serve label. It is also the only cocktail with a tasting note, so the four cocktail entries speak in two voices.
'hop-forward draft IPA' repeats 'draft' from the De Barril · Draft subhead right above it.
Brut Rosé 13 prints with no glass or bottle label, and the draft label is empty. It is flagged correctly (needs_input 5), but a guest cannot tell what 13 buys.

Cider is a separate section in the draft (sec_cider, which comes after Spirits). It is printed under 'Cerveza y Sidra · Beer & Cider' and then gets its own 'Sidra · Cider' subhead, so 'Sidra' appears twice in 90 pt. The move is noted (meta.printed_under), so it is not an integrity fail, but it is redundant.

Items were reordered inside subs (Margarita before Manhattan; Old Fashioned before Daiquiri), and 'House Originals' was renamed 'De la Casa · House'. Both are defensible for a cantina and nothing was dropped, but the renaming is undisclosed in the doc diff apart from proposal.md.

The draft title 'Bar menu' becomes the wordmark 'CANTINA' plus the rail line '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA'. That is venue descriptors, not an item fact, so the gate passes. But if 'Cantina' is not the venue's actual name, it prints as a brand name nobody supplied. Confirm with Rob.

Daiquiri ingredient line breaks after 'fresh lime ·', leaving a short first line and a long second line. The Margarita and Old Fashioned breaks are also unmanaged. Criterion 5 flow is correct in order (Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits), but there is no non-alcoholic section. It is not in the draft and has been asked, but for a Mexican restaurant (agua fresca, Jarritos) the gap is visible.

Price column (criterion 3): tabular, no $, a single right edge at 576 pt, and a dotted leader on every row. But Margarita and Manhattan travel 0.66-0.68 of the measure to reach their prices, the widest on the page, on the two lead items. Leaders keep the association gate a pass, but it is long eye travel on the hero rows.
fixes: Replace the three spirits echo-descriptors with nothing but a flagged placeholder style (or a sourced serve fact such as a pour size once Rob answers), so no row repeats its own name; set every descriptor in one case (lower case: 'vsop cognac' or drop).
Move 'Bright and citrus-forward.' to sit directly after the Margarita ingredients (before the ROCKS label), or drop it so all four cocktails share one voice: ingredients · garnish · GLASS.
Drop the redundant 'Sidra · Cider' subhead, or rename the section head 'Cerveza · Beer' and keep 'Sidra · Cider' as its sub, so 'Sidra' prints once; and cut 'draft' from 'hop-forward draft IPA'.

Balance the cocktail ingredient-line breaks by hand (for example 'white rum · fresh lime · house demerara syrup ·' / 'lime coin · COUPE') and shorten the Margarita/Manhattan leader span by pulling the price column in or narrowing the cocktail measure.

Before print, get Rob's answers on the Brut Rosé glass/bottle label, beer and cider ABV, wine region, spirit brand, and whether 'CANTINA' is the venue's real name, then print them as `style · ABV`, `grape · region` and `brand · age` in the existing descriptor lane.

lens: ingredient names and description completeness (checked against the round-1 draft snapshot doc.json, round-19 doc.json/proposal.md and preview-letter.png)
top_problem: Below the cocktails, the descriptions mostly repeat the item names. 'Blanco Tequila: blanco tequila', 'Añejo Tequila: añejo tequila', 'Cognac VSOP: VSOP Cognac', 'Dry Cider: dry sparkling cider', 'Brut Rosé: dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry-Hopped IPA: hop-forward draft IPA' and 'Amber Lager: toasty amber lager' each spend a line saying what the name already says. Ten of the fourteen items therefore give the guest almost no new fact. The known data gap (beer ABV and brewery, wine region and producer, spirit brand, age statement and pour size) is not the designer's fault: Rob has been asked and proposal.md tabulates it in needs_input 2-6. But the descriptors the designer chose to print around that gap are padding, not description.
problems: Checked against the draft: all 14 items and all 14 prices match exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, House Daiquiri 14, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18). Nothing is invented and nothing is dropped. The round-17 taglines and kickers are gone. The only rail text left is '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA', which is venue identity and states no item fact.

Cocktails are close to complete: spirit, modifiers, garnish and a sourced glass on all four. But the Manhattan prints 'rye' where the component is 'Rye Whiskey'. On its own 'rye' is ambiguous (a grain or a whiskey), and the Margarita's 'tequila blanco' spells out its spirit, so the Manhattan's base spirit is the least clear of the four.

Hiding the Manhattan's aromatic bitters is correct under meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false} and is not a fault. But the Old Fashioned prints 'aromatic bitters' two items below, which makes the omission look like a mistake to a trained reader. needs_input 11 is the right flag and should stay open.

Spirits: the category's fixed age definitions (for example, añejo means aged in oak for at least one year) are the one extra fact that is available without a brand, and the menu does not use them. The draft snapshot's own spirits text ('Añejo (aged) class', 'VSOP age grade') was reduced to an echo of the name.
Wine: 'Malbec: dry red wine' and 'Pinot Grigio: dry white wine' state the colour and nothing else. Region and producer are the known data gap and are properly flagged.

Brut Rosé sits under 'Espumosos · Sparkling', outside the 'Por Copa · By the Glass' heading, and its 13 has no glass or bottle label. It is correctly flagged as needs_input 5, but a guest cannot tell what 13 buys. It does not fail the association gate, but it is a real content ambiguity.

Voice: every line is lower case with no full stop, except the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.', which is a capitalised sentence with a full stop. It is the only tasting note on the menu, so the Margarita reads as having a different writer.
'De Barril · Draft' heads the beers, so the word 'draft' in 'hop-forward draft IPA' says the same thing twice.
The House Daiquiri ingredient line breaks after 'white rum · fresh lime ·', leaving a short first line and the syrup pushed to line two. Among the cocktail lines it has the weakest rag.

Section order (Cocktails → Beer & Cider → Wine → Spirits) is standard and every drinks category gets the same H2/H3 treatment. For a Mexican cantina, the absence of a mezcal, a Mexican lager and any non-alcoholic option is conspicuous. It is correctly asked in needs_input 7 rather than invented.
fixes: Where the name already says everything, stop echoing it. Print one sourced category fact instead (for example, 'añejo tequila' becomes 'aged in oak at least one year', and 'VSOP Cognac' becomes 'grape brandy, VSOP age grade', which is draft snapshot wording), or leave the line blank until needs_input 2-6 return ABV, region, brand and age.
Change the Manhattan's 'rye' to 'rye whiskey' to match the component 'Rye Whiskey', so the base spirit is as clear as the Margarita's 'tequila blanco'.

Give the Brut Rosé price a label, or move the Brut Rosé under the glass header once needs_input 5 is answered. Until then, add a small 'glass or bottle' placeholder that the Coordinator can see in the proof, so 13 cannot ship ambiguous.

Bring the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' into the menu's voice (lower case, no full stop, for example 'bright, citrus-forward'), or print one sourced tasting note on each cocktail, so that one drink does not read as written by a different hand.
Cut the redundant 'draft' from 'hop-forward draft IPA' and rebalance the House Daiquiri line break so that 'house demerara syrup' stays on the first line.

lens: flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The section heads do not outrank the items, and the lower half reads as a stock list. The H2s are 13 pt caps with the Spanish half light, and they read no stronger than the 11 pt bold tracked item names. MARGARITA is visually as loud as CÓCTELES · COCKTAILS, so there is no single clear entry below the wordmark. Everything below the cocktails is one-row entries whose descriptor just repeats the name ('Blanco Tequila / blanco tequila', 'Cognac VSOP / VSOP Cognac', 'Dry-Hopped IPA / hop-forward draft IPA'). For a cantina, the agave category comes last, with two unbranded tequilas and no mezcal. The eye has nothing to land on after the Daiquiri.
problems: Weak H2-to-item hierarchy (criterion 5). The H2 is 13 pt caps with the Spanish half at weight 420 in #4F4238; item names are Fraunces 600 at 11 pt, tracked caps. Section breaks come mainly from the 18 pt gap and the hairline rule, not from type rank, so four sections and 14 names all compete at close to the same level.

Rhythm break (criteria 5 and 10). The cocktails get 2-3 line blocks, and all 10 remaining items drop to one-row entries. This groups the page but makes the bottom 60% read as an inventory. The Spirits block, the cantina's natural signature, is the thinnest and last.

Name-echo descriptors (criterion 8). 'blanco tequila', 'añejo tequila' and 'VSOP Cognac' only restate the item name, and 'hop-forward draft IPA', 'dry red wine' and 'dry white wine' add almost nothing. These are faithful to the draft, but printing them fills space with no information.

Known data gap, not the designer's fault: beer ABV, wine region and producer, and spirit brand and age are missing. proposal.md tabulates them correctly as needs_input 2, 4 and 6. Until Rob fills them, no non-cocktail item can meet the criterion-8 standard (style + ABV, grape + region, type/age + brand), so criterion 8 is capped.

The Margarita is the only cocktail with a tasting-note sentence ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). It is capitalised and has a full stop, while every other line is lower-case with no stop. Its ROCKS glass label also sits mid-block, between the ingredients and the sentence, where on the other cocktails it ends the block (criterion 10).

Awkward line breaks in the cocktail block. The House Daiquiri breaks after 'white rum · fresh lime ·', leaving a short first line and a long second one. The Margarita breaks after 'orange liqueur ·'. Both ragged breaks weaken the scan.
Brut Rosé 13 prints with no glass/bottle label, correctly flagged as needs_input 5. Until it is answered, the wine price column is ambiguous for that row (criterion 3).

No non-alcoholic section and no mezcal. These are absent from the draft and correctly asked for as needs_input 7, so this is not a designer fault. Still, the page lacks the category a Mexican cantina guest expects.

Tagline audit: the side rail now holds only the vertical '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' line (venue identity, no item fact), and the kickers are gone, so it passes. The printed venue name 'Cantina' is not in the draft title ('Bar menu'). It is flagged as needs_input 8 and must be confirmed before print.

Prices: 14 of 14 match (15, 15, 16, 14 / 7, 8, 7, 8 / 12, 11, 13 / 12, 16, 18). There is one right-aligned tabular column with dotted leaders on every row; the maximum eye travel is 0.68 and it has a leader. No item was dropped or invented, and Junmai Ginjo is left off with a note.
fixes: Make the H2 clearly outrank the item names. Raise it to about 16-18 pt, set the English half at display weight, and drop the item names to about 10 pt at weight 500-600, so each section head is a distinct second focal level below CANTINA.

Where the draft descriptor only repeats the name (the three spirits), print no descriptor, or a quiet '—' / 'ask your server' placeholder, until Rob supplies brand and age. Keep 'crisp pale lager' and 'toasty amber lager', which do add style.

Make the Margarita block match the others. Move ROCKS to the end of the whole block, and either set 'Bright and citrus-forward.' as a lower-case italic note with no stop, or add sourced notes to all four cocktails and not just one.
Rebalance the ingredient-line breaks so the first line is the longer one: 'white rum · fresh lime · house demerara syrup ·' / 'lime coin · COUPE', and likewise for the Margarita.

Once needs_input 2, 4, 5 and 6 are answered, restore two-line rows for beer, wine and spirits (style · ABV, grape · region, brand · age) and add a glass/bottle price label. This round's one-row format is a placeholder and should not become the permanent pattern.

lens: Voice and consistency of descriptions, bilingual headings, venue copy and venue-type fit (Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: Outside the four cocktails, the descriptions mostly repeat the item's name instead of describing the drink. BLANCO TEQUILA says 'blanco tequila', AÑEJO TEQUILA says 'añejo tequila', COGNAC VSOP says 'VSOP Cognac', AMBER LAGER says 'toasty amber lager' and DRY CIDER says 'dry sparkling cider'. At a cantina the agave pours should carry the most voice, and here they carry none. The missing beer ABV, wine region and spirit brand are an open data gap: it is already asked of Rob and tabulated in proposal.md, so it is not the designer's fault. But printing the item name back as a description is the designer's choice. Other problems: (a) The voice is split. The Margarita alone gets a sentence-case tasting note with a full stop ('Bright and citrus-forward.'), set in the same roman as its ingredient list, so it reads as a run-on. The house signatures (De la Casa) get no tasting note at all. (b) The same syrup is written two ways. The Old Fashioned says 'demerara syrup' and the Daiquiri says 'house demerara syrup', although the Old Fashioned component's role is 'House prep / sweetener', so 'house' is sourced for both. (c) Word order is mixed: 'tequila blanco' in the Margarita line but 'BLANCO TEQUILA' as a spirit name. (d) The bilingual hierarchy prints the Spanish half light grey and the English half heavy black. At a Mexican venue this makes the Spanish look like trim rather than a shared voice, which contradicts the round-19 thesis. The proposal also says 'every label' is bilingual, but 'Agave' and 'Brandy' print in one language only. (e) The ROCKS/COUPE glass labels use the same '·' separator as the ingredients, so the glass reads as one more ingredient. (f) The Brut Rosé price of 13 has no glass or bottle label, and 'Espumosos' does not say which (needs_input 5). (g) The 'CANTINA' wordmark and '& COCKTAIL BAR' line replace the draft title 'Bar menu'. They are venue copy, not item facts, so no gate fails, but they stay unconfirmed until needs_input 8 is answered. All 14 prices match the round-19 doc.json and proposal.md copy table (15/15/16/14/7/8/7/8/12/11/13/12/16/18). No tagline states an item fact, and every price sits on its name row with a leader.
fixes: Stop printing the item name back as its description: set spirits as name plus price only (or name plus category, e.g. BLANCO TEQUILA 'unaged 100% agave' only if sourced) until brand and age arrive, and rewrite the beer and cider lines so they add a fact the name does not already give.

Make the voice one rule: either give every cocktail, De la Casa first, a short sourced tasting note in italic on its own line, or drop the Margarita's note, and never set a sentence-case note in the same roman as a lower-case ingredient list.

Write the syrup the same way on both cocktails ('house demerara syrup'; the Old Fashioned component's role 'House prep' sources it) and use one word order for tequila across the menu (for example 'blanco tequila' in the Margarita line to match the spirit rows).

Give the Spanish and English halves of each bilingual heading equal weight (same weight, contrast set by the colour of the dot or the case), so the Spanish does not read as a grey caption at a Mexican venue, and correct the proposal's claim that every label is bilingual ('Agave' and 'Brandy' are not).

Set the glass off from the ingredients with a different separator or a line of its own (for example an em space and small caps with no '·'), and add a glass or bottle label to the Brut Rosé once needs_input 5 is answered.

lens: missing data: how the known gaps (missing_ingredients, allergy line, Brut Rosé glass vs bottle) are flagged, and whether anything was invented to cover them
top_problem: The gaps are well flagged in the data and invisible on the page, and the page quietly settles one of them. Nothing is invented. doc.json meta.missing and the proposal list brewery/ABV/pour, producer/region/vintage, brand/age and needs_input 1, 4, 5, 11. But the printed page lets thin data show as thin copy. BLANCO TEQUILA 'blanco tequila', AÑEJO TEQUILA 'añejo tequila' and COGNAC VSOP 'VSOP Cognac' only repeat the item name. The beers have no ABV and the wines have no region, so criterion 8 fails its own definition on 7 of 14 items. The worst case is Brut Rosé. It prints an unlabelled 13, in the same price column and at the same weight, one line below two 'Por Copa · By the Glass' rows. A guest will read it as a $13 glass, which is the very fact needs_input 5 has not answered, so the layout implies an unconfirmed serve. The allergy line 'Please tell your server about any allergies.' is generic and makes no item claim, so it is acceptable. However, it sits in the same italic voice and position as a footnote and does not point to the unconfirmed dairy in the Brown Butter Old Fashioned. The big 'CANTINA' wordmark replaces the draft title 'Bar menu' and is still an open question (needs_input 8), not a confirmed venue name.
fixes: Do not publish Brut Rosé with an unlabelled price. Until needs_input 5 is answered, hold the print. Once answered, add an explicit 'copa' or 'botella' label in the price column (or a 'glass | bottle' column header for all wine) so it cannot inherit 'By the Glass' by proximity.

Stop spirit descriptions from repeating the item name: set the category once in the H3 ('Agave' / 'Brandy'). Leave the descriptor slot empty or use the flagged unknown (brand, age statement, pour) as a visible 'ask your server' cue rather than echoing 'blanco tequila'/'VSOP Cognac'. Chase needs_input 6 so real brand and age can print.

Put the missing beer ABV and wine region on the venue's critical path (needs_input 2 and 4). Criterion 8 cannot rise above the high 50s while beer shows no ABV and wine shows no region, however clean the typography.

Keep the generic allergy line. Also resolve needs_input 1 (dairy in the brown butter-washed bourbon) before print so the house cocktail's allergen status is either confirmed on the line or deliberately left to the server; an unconfirmed allergen should not be left open on a finished menu.

Tidy the voice so the gaps do not look like inconsistencies: 'AGAVE' and 'BRANDY' are the only English-only H3s on a bilingual page (use 'Agave' plus 'Brandy · Brandy', or explain why they are exempt), and 'Bright and citrus-forward.' is the only sentence-case line in a lower-case system. Also confirm with the venue (needs_input 8) that 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' may replace the draft title before it prints 96 pt tall.

lens: I traced every printed ingredient, garnish, glass label and heading to build/draft_doc.json and to phg.recipe_versions through the gateway (log_id 255, joined on phg.menu_items.current_recipe_version_id). I also checked description quality, venue fit and how descriptions and prices sit together.

Every garnish and glass traces to a real row: Margarita lime wheel/Rocks (rv f06abb74), Manhattan cocktail cherry/Coupe (rv 9fb77eaa), Brown Butter Old Fashioned orange peel/Rocks (rv 7095fd3d), House Daiquiri lime coin/Coupe (rv 14d45e57). But 9 of the 15 items print a description that only repeats the item name, which is the automatic-fail condition for criterion 12: Blanco Tequila 'blanco tequila', Añejo Tequila 'añejo tequila', Cognac VSOP 'VSOP Cognac', Amber Lager 'toasty amber lager', Dry-Hopped IPA 'hop-forward draft IPA', Dry Cider 'dry sparkling cider', Brut Rosé 'dry sparkling rosé', Malbec 'dry red wine' and Pinot Grigio 'dry white wine' (the last two are the grape's category, not a description). The CANTINA wordmark and the correct bilingual heads (Cócteles, De Barril, Por Copa, Espumosos, Destilados) are doing the work the list does not do. (e) Data drift: menu_items holds 'Junmai Ginjo' ($12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.') for this project, but it is absent from draft_doc.json and from the print. The Coordinator should resolve whether the draft or the DB is stale. The ABV, region and brand gaps are the known pending items Rob has been asked to fill and are not scored as invented.
fixes: Replace the name-echo descriptions as soon as Rob's brand, producer, region, ABV and age rows land (for example grape plus region for the wines, brand plus agave/age statement for the tequilas, brewery plus style plus ABV for the beers); until then, print nothing rather than an echo of the name, and flag them missing_ingredients.

Restore 'aromatic bitters' to the Manhattan line (source: menu_items.menu_description for bf732e78 and the draft component 'Aromatic Bitters'), or get needs_input 11 answered in writing, so the classic doesn't read as incomplete.

Make the cocktail voice one rule: either drop the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' or give every cocktail a sourced one-line note; add the missing separator after ROCKS in doc.json's Margarita desc.
Label the Brut Rosé price (glass or bottle) and add pour sizes for the tequila and Cognac pours, the draft beers and the by-the-glass wines once supplied; a guest must never guess what $13 buys.

Designer/Coordinator note on venue fit (item lists are not mine to change): a Mexican cantina needs agave to lead, so ask Rob for mezcal and Mexican-lager rows, and consider moving Destilados/Agave ahead of Wine.

lens: description quality and one guest-facing voice (criteria 10-14), TEST-1 round 19
top_problem: The descriptions are still the draft's shorthand, not guest copy. Three of the 14 printed items only repeat their own name: BLANCO TEQUILA 'blanco tequila', AÑEJO TEQUILA 'añejo tequila' and COGNAC VSOP 'VSOP Cognac' (phg.menu_items menu_description 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'; gateway log_id 251). That triggers the automatic cap on criterion 12. Four more are taxonomy labels rather than appetising copy: Malbec 'dry red wine', Pinot Grigio 'dry white wine', Amber Lager 'toasty amber lager' and Dry-Hopped IPA 'hop-forward draft IPA', where 'draft' repeats the De Barril head. The voice is also split three ways: lower-case ingredient fragments; bold tracked glass words (ROCKS, COUPE) that read as a fifth ingredient; and one capitalised full sentence ('Bright and citrus-forward.'), which only the Margarita gets and which is printed after its glass label. Separately, content_integrity fails because the project's phg.menu_items has a 15th priced item, Junmai Ginjo ($12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.', log_id 251). It is missing from doc.json and from the printed menu, and nobody flagged it. What I verified: every printed ingredient, garnish and glass traces to a source (garnish and glassware from phg.recipe_versions via current_recipe_version_id, log_id 251: Margarita Rocks / Lime wheel, Manhattan Coupe / Cocktail cherry, House Daiquiri Coupe / Lime coin, Brown Butter Old Fashioned Rocks / Orange peel). The ingredients 'fresh lime', 'agave syrup' and 'house demerara syrup' trace to the doc.json components (Fresh Lime Juice, Agave Syrup, and Demerara Syrup with the note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup by weight.'). All 14 printed prices match menu_price. Criterion 11 still stays at 72 because of the known gap: no ABV, brewery, region, brand, pour size or age on any beer, wine or spirit. Criterion 13: the bilingual heads use correct accents and idiomatic Spanish (Cócteles, De Barril, Por Copa, Espumosos, Destilados), and $7-18 fits Iowa City. But the list does not read as a Mexican cantina: two tequilas and no mezcal, European-style beers, and Malbec and Pinot Grigio. The copy does nothing to anchor the items to the venue, and the heads' Spanish is the only cultural voice. Criterion 14: the leaders keep every price tied to its item, so menu_item_association passes. The weak points are the House Daiquiri break (a short 'white rum · fresh lime ·' over a long second line), the tasting note sitting under the glass label, and the name-echo pairs, which look like stutters in the one-row format.
fixes: Resolve Junmai Ginjo ($12, phg.menu_items, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.'): print it (for example as 'Sake' under Vino, or as its own sub) or have the Coordinator confirm in writing that it is dropped from this draft. Until then content_integrity stays a fail.

Replace the three name-echo spirit lines with a sourced, non-repeating fact (agave type, age statement, producer or region from brands/products/spirit_lexicon once Rob supplies the brand). If none is available, print the name alone with no echo line rather than repeating it.

Give every item one guest-voice pattern: either every cocktail gets a short sourced tasting note like the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.', or the Margarita's note moves to directly under the name and before the ingredient line so it is not stranded after ROCKS.

Take the glass words out of the ingredient run: set them as a separate, lighter serve cue (for example right-aligned under the price or as a quiet trailing label with more space), so ROCKS and COUPE stop reading as ingredients. Rebalance the House Daiquiri break to two even lines; send the layout part to the designer as a note.

When Rob's ABV, brewery, region and grape data lands, replace 'dry red wine', 'dry white wine', 'toasty amber lager' and 'hop-forward draft IPA' with guest copy of region, producer and ABV (for example 'Mendoza · 13.5%'), and drop the 'draft' that repeats the De Barril head.

lens: Venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, IA (census context, bilingual headings), plus ingredient trace and description/price layout
top_problem: The Spanish headings make it look like a cantina, but the list itself still reads like a generic American cocktail bar. Only 1 of the 4 cocktails uses agave (Margarita). The 'De la Casa · House' tier is a bourbon Old Fashioned and a rum Daiquiri. Agave spirits sit last, under Malbec and Pinot Grigio. The beer list is Czech Pilsner, IPA and Amber Lager. Nearly every beer, wine and spirit description repeats its item name ('blanco tequila', 'añejo tequila', 'VSOP Cognac', 'toasty amber lager', 'hop-forward draft IPA'). That means criterion 12 is near its auto-fail line, and nothing in the layout offsets the agave-light list. Evidence: the gateway query (log_id 250) found every printed fact in phg.menu_items.menu_description or phg.recipe_versions (glass: f06abb74 Rocks, 9fb77eaa Coupe, 14d45e57 Coupe, 7095fd3d Rocks; garnish: Lime wheel, Cocktail cherry, Lime coin, Orange peel). The Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' is from menu_item 14555870. 'Junmai Ginjo' (57617f46) is status 'retired' and not in the draft doc (log_id 257), so leaving it off is correct. Census (phg_census_zcta, ACS 2020-2024): 52240 is 11.0% Hispanic/Latino, median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree, median household income $52,960. 52246 is 8.3% Hispanic, 36.9% aged 21-34, $62,521. 52245 is 5.4% Hispanic, $78,020. That is a young university crowd, mostly non-Spanish-speaking and price-sensitive. So English-weighted bilingual labels are the right call, but $14-16 cocktails with no lower-priced agave entry point sit at the top of this town's price tier. The known gap stands: no ABV, region, brewery/brand or pour size on beer, wine or spirits (menu_items 90b0a7e3, 8fb136cd, 70657e1e, Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé, the two tequilas, Cognac VSOP), so those rows cannot score above the low 70s until Rob supplies the data. The bilingual system is also inconsistent: 'AGAVE' and 'BRANDY' have no Spanish · English pair, while every other label does.
fixes: Move DESTILADOS · SPIRITS (Agave first) up to follow the cocktails, ahead of beer and wine, so the cantina's category leads the page. Use Cocktails, then Agave spirits, then Cerveza, then Vino. This is an order change only; no items change.

Once Rob supplies the data, replace every description that repeats its item name with sourced facts (tequila brand and NOM or region, age statement; beer brewery, style and ABV; wine grape and region). Until then, keep those rows name-plus-price only rather than echoing the name back in lower case.

Pair the last two subheads like every other label (for example 'Agave · Agave' becomes 'Destilados de Agave · Agave', and 'Brandy' gets a Spanish pair). Otherwise the bilingual rule reads as broken exactly where the menu should be most Mexican.

Use one description voice. Either make the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' a lower-case ingredient-line tail, or give every cocktail a sourced tasting line. The sentence also sits under the ROCKS glass tag and reads as an orphaned third line; put the glass tag after the note, or put the note first.

Tighten the cocktail rag. The House Daiquiri breaks after 'white rum · fresh lime ·', leaving a stub first line, and the Margarita breaks after 'orange liqueur ·'. Balance the breaks to two even lines, and add pour labels (pint/oz for draft, 2 oz for spirits) as soon as the missing 'pour size' flags are filled.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png (criterion 14 and the menu_item_association gate), plus accuracy criteria 10-13. Sources: gateway log_id 253 (phg.menu_items joined to phg.recipe_versions for project ddc4bb5b) and log_id 254 (phg_census_zcta 52240/52245/52246). Known gap: ABV, region and brand are missing and Rob has been asked for them. They are not scored as invented facts.
top_problem: A draft item is missing from the print. The draft has Junmai Ginjo (phg.menu_items 57617f46, $12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.'), but it is not in the print, doc.json or proposal.md, and nothing says it was removed on purpose. That fails content_integrity. Every printed fact does check out: all 14 printed prices match menu_items.menu_price, and the glasses and garnishes match recipe_versions f06abb74 (Rocks, Lime wheel), 9fb77eaa (Coupe, Cocktail cherry), 7095fd3d (Rocks, Orange peel) and 14d45e57 (Coupe, Lime coin). The price-to-item link also holds: every price sits on its name's line with a dotted leader, in one right-aligned column (spread 0.0 pt), and every description sits directly under or beside its own item. So menu_item_association passes. The next biggest drag is criterion 12. All seven one-row descriptions in wine and spirits and four of the five in beer and cider only repeat the item name: 'Blanco Tequila / blanco tequila', 'Añejo Tequila / añejo tequila', 'Cognac VSOP / VSOP Cognac', 'Amber Lager / toasty amber lager', 'Dry Cider / dry sparkling cider', 'Dry-Hopped IPA / hop-forward draft IPA', 'Brut Rosé / dry sparkling rosé'. The spirits lines are the draft text (menu_items 19d79518, 124f8949, 75501d63) with 'pour' removed, which makes them exact echoes of the name. The wine lines 'dry red wine' and 'dry white wine' (f6f9d57e, 5ba7511f) read as category labels. That is the scorecard's automatic fail for repeating the name. Layout faults (criterion 14): (a) The House Daiquiri breaks after 'white rum · fresh lime ·', so line 1 fills only about 40% of the measure and line 2 is heavy. (b) The Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' is a third line in the same roman as the lowercase ingredient list, so it reads as more ingredients. It is also the only tasting note on the menu, so the voice is inconsistent. (c) ROCKS and COUPE are glued to the end of the ingredient line with no label or space of their own, so the glass reads as one more ingredient. (d) Spirits and beer rows have no pour or measure label, and the wine glass price is labelled only by the 'Por Copa' subhead. (e) Cocktail descriptions stop at about 75 mm of a 104 mm column, while the one-row items squeeze their descriptions between name and leader with barely a word space and no change of weight or colour. Venue fit (criterion 13): the bilingual heads are correct and fully accented, but this is supposed to be a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar. It has one agave cocktail, no mezcal, no Mexican beer, and gives the house slot to a bourbon Old Fashioned. Cocktails at $14-16 sit at the top of the market for ZCTA 52240 (median household income $52,960, median age 28.6).
fixes: Account for Junmai Ginjo (menu_items 57617f46, $12). Either print it with its draft text 'Junmai Ginjo sake.' or get the Coordinator to record its removal in doc.json and proposal.md; until then content_integrity stays failed.

Replace the descriptions that only repeat the name with sourced guest language. For spirits, restore the draft word 'pour' and add the pour size once Rob supplies it. For wine and beer, add grape, region, style and ABV once Rob supplies them. If a fact is still missing, print only the name and price instead of an echo line.

Move the glass label out of the ingredient string onto its own consistent slot, such as a small-caps tag right-aligned under the price or a fixed column on the name row, so ROCKS and COUPE are clearly serve information, not ingredients.
Fix the rag: rebreak the House Daiquiri so line 1 fills at least 70% of the measure. Set 'Bright and citrus-forward.' in italic or a distinct tone, or drop it so the four cocktails share one voice.

Give the one-row descriptions a clear gap (at least 2 em) and a lighter colour or weight than the name, and label the pour sizes ('2 oz', '16 oz', '5 oz' by the glass) once Rob supplies them, so every price says what it buys.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together on the phone preview (preview-phone.png), plus ingredient sourcing and venue fit

That item is not in doc.json, menu.html or the preview, and proposal.md does not mention it, so content_integrity fails because an item is missing with no note (doc.json is revision 3, synced 2026-09-23, so it is behind the draft). The draft does have that text (menu_items.menu_description), so it is sourced, but criterion 12 fails those rows outright. The missing ABV, region and brand (already with Rob) is why they read as filler. Verified as correct against phg.recipe_versions: Margarita f06abb74 (Rocks, Lime wheel), Manhattan 9fb77eaa (Coupe, Cocktail cherry), House Daiquiri 14d45e57 (Coupe, Lime coin; 'house demerara syrup' matches menu_description 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.'), Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d (Rocks, Orange peel). fixes: Add Junmai Ginjo ($12, menu_items 'Junmai Ginjo sake.') back to the doc and the page, or get a written removal decision from Rob and note it in proposal.md; until then content_integrity stays failed.

Replace the description lines that repeat the name on the spirits, wine, beer and cider rows with sourced facts (ABV, region, grape, brand, agave or age statement) once Rob supplies them; until then, drop those lines and flag missing_ingredients rather than print filler, which is what caps criterion 12.

Designer: on phone, keep the glass label last by putting 'Bright and citrus-forward.' above the ingredient line (or merging it into the lower-case voice), and put the glass behind a small labelled prefix or icon so ROCKS and COUPE don't read as ingredients.
Designer: stop the phone header wrap by tying the '·' to 'BEER & CIDER' or setting that H2 on a tighter track, and rebalance the Manhattan break so no line is under a third of the measure.

For venue fit, ask Rob whether the draft can take a mezcal, a Mexican lager and a non-alcoholic section (without inventing any), and make 'Agave' and 'Brandy' follow the same Spanish · English pattern as the other subheads.
